title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
description: Ten documented Oakland University rituals, recurring events, and ceremonial customs—with historical items clearly labeled.

cards.title: Celebrate the founder's birthday
cards.subtitle: Annual October campus celebration
cards.notes: Look for the October Birthday Bash honoring founder Matilda Dodge Wilson; use the event as a prompt to explore the university’s Meadow Brook roots.
cards.short_summary: Oakland’s founder is still celebrated with an annual campus birthday event.
cards.evidence_claim: Oakland University’s alumni publication says the annual Matilda’s Birthday Bash continues as a campus event highlight.
cards.source_title: Then and Now: The OUAA’s 50-Year Journey
cards.access_notes: Check Oakland University’s event listings for the current year’s program and attendance details.

cards.title: Dress up for Meadow Brook Ball
cards.subtitle: Meadow Brook Hall student tradition since 1974
cards.notes: Watch for committee announcements and, if attending, plan around the formal evening at Meadow Brook Hall with food, dancing, and entertainment.
cards.short_summary: A student-organized formal at Meadow Brook Hall that dates to 1974.
cards.evidence_claim: Oakland University’s Student Involvement directory identifies Meadow Brook Ball as one of OU’s oldest traditions and says its committee has hosted it since 1974.
cards.access_notes: Event participation and ticketing details vary by year; consult the Meadow Brook Ball Committee’s current announcements.

cards.entity_name: The Rock near the Oakland Center
cards.title: Add your mark to the Rock
cards.subtitle: Near the Oakland Center
cards.notes: See the painted Rock near the student center and follow current university guidance before participating; its changing layers preserve a long-running student practice.
cards.short_summary: Painting the Rock is recorded among Oakland student traditions.
cards.evidence_claim: Oakland University’s alumni publication lists painting the rock near the student center among remembered OU traditions.
cards.source_title: Then and Now: The OUAA’s 50-Year Journey
cards.access_notes: Confirm any current painting rules or event permissions with Oakland University before adding paint.

cards.entity_name: Midnight Walk to Meadow Brook Hall
cards.title: Remember the Midnight Walk
cards.subtitle: Historic first-year orientation tradition
cards.notes: Treat this as a documented historical orientation tradition: the walk paired new students with alumni-led stories and legends around Meadow Brook Hall.
cards.short_summary: A historic overnight-orientation walk introduced newcomers to campus legends.
cards.evidence_claim: Oakland University documented the Midnight Walk as a distinctly OU tradition during first-year orientation, including a Legends, Myths, and Tales Tour.
cards.source_title: OU legends abound at Midnight Walk to Meadow Brook Hall
cards.access_notes: Historical item: the source documents a 2013 orientation activity; do not assume it is currently offered.

cards.title: Climb Elliott Tower as a senior
cards.subtitle: Elliott Tower graduation ritual
cards.notes: If you are an eligible graduating student, follow the university’s current instructions for the Senior Climb, commemorative photo, and tower-signing tradition.
cards.short_summary: Graduates climb Elliott Tower, photograph the moment, and sign their names.
cards.evidence_claim: Oakland University reports that graduates take part in the Senior Climb by climbing Elliott Tower’s steps, taking a commemorative photo, and signing their names.
cards.access_notes: Eligibility and scheduling are event-specific; verify current Senior Climb details with Oakland University.

cards.title: Join the Golden Grizzly Clap-In
cards.subtitle: Elliott Tower to the O’rena
cards.notes: At New Student Welcome, faculty, staff, and student leaders line the route from Elliott Tower to the O’rena to clap in incoming Grizzlies.
cards.short_summary: New students enter their official welcome through a campus Clap-In.
cards.evidence_claim: Oakland University describes New Student Welcome as a long-standing tradition and identifies its Clap-In route from Elliott Tower to the O’rena.
cards.source_title: Volunteers sought for New Student Welcome event
cards.access_notes: This is tied to the fall New Student Welcome; check the current orientation schedule for participation details.

cards.title: Make a film in 24 hours
cards.subtitle: Film and Theatre programs
cards.notes: Form a team for the annual challenge, then shoot and edit a short film within 24 hours using your own gear or designated program resources.
cards.short_summary: OU teams create short films on a one-day production clock.
cards.evidence_claim: Oakland University calls the 24-Hour Film Challenge an important annual tradition of its Film and Theatre programs.
cards.source_title: Oakland University hosts 11th annual 24-Hour Film Challenge
cards.access_notes: The 2025 event used Varner Hall editing lab 228; confirm current challenge dates, equipment access, and submission rules.

cards.title: Mark Hispanic Heritage Month at OU
cards.subtitle: September 15–October 15 campus observance
cards.notes: Follow the Center for Multicultural Initiatives’ annual program of talks and events recognizing Hispanic histories, politics, culture, and contributions.
cards.short_summary: OU maintains a long-standing campus observance of Hispanic Heritage Month.
cards.evidence_claim: Oakland University states that recognizing National Hispanic Heritage Month is a long-standing OU tradition.
cards.source_title: Oakland University celebrates National Hispanic Heritage Month
cards.access_notes: Programming changes annually; consult the Center for Multicultural Initiatives’ current event schedule.

cards.title: Spot the oak-and-obsidian mace
cards.subtitle: Commencement and convocation ceremonial processional
cards.notes: At a university ceremony, look for the marshal carrying OU’s scepter mace; it signals the arrival of the faculty processional.
cards.short_summary: OU’s distinctive mace leads major academic ceremonies.
cards.evidence_claim: Oakland University says its mace, created in 1994, is carried at commencement, convocation, and other ceremonies to signify the faculty processional’s arrival.
cards.access_notes: Observe this ceremonial tradition during a public commencement or convocation; access follows the particular event’s attendance policies.

cards.title: Attend the President’s Colloquium
cards.subtitle: Annual faculty scholarship lecture series
cards.notes: Watch for the annual colloquium and attend a faculty presentation that connects scholarly work with broad questions across science, history, politics, or humanities.
cards.short_summary: A yearly lecture tradition showcasing Oakland faculty scholarship.
cards.evidence_claim: Oakland University states that the President’s Colloquium began in 1995 and is an annual Oakland tradition centered on faculty academic and research work.
cards.access_notes: The source documents the annual series; verify the current year’s speaker, venue, and public attendance information.

warnings: The Midnight Walk is explicitly labeled historical because the direct source documents its 2013 orientation use rather than a current offering.
The President’s Colloquium source documents the annual tradition but predates the template freshness window; current scheduling should be confirmed.
